subject: Procurement intake & vendor setup — next steps (PO vs card)

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement intake & vendor setup — next steps (PO vs card)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the procurement side so we can keep the timeline to your end-of-quarter rollout: 

1) Vendor setup: Acme typically needs a vendor packet (W-9, banking details, remittance info). I can attach our packet and W-9 to this thread.
2) Procurement path: You mentioned the team prefers PO-based purchases for platform subscriptions. We accept both PO (net 30/45) and credit card depending on the agreement. If PO, do you need a signed SOW + invoice or a standalone commercial agreement?
3) Marketplace: Are you interested in transacting through AWS Marketplace? We can list/purchase there which simplifies procurement for some customers but changes billing terms (Marketplace handles payments).
4) Next steps: I can share the vendor packet and a draft SOW for your legal/procurement review. If you prefer, we can open a DocuSign for the SOW and provide invoice terms.

Attaching: Redwood_Vendor_Packet_v1.pdf, Redwood_W-9.pdf, SOW-draft.docx (draft).

Can you confirm: (a) primary procurement contact for vendor setup, (b) whether Acme requires vendor forms in a specific portal (link?), and (c) preference for PO vs card?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call with your procurement lead if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement intake & vendor setup — next steps (PO vs card)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and for sending the attachments. A few answers from procurement: 

- Primary procurement contact: procurement@acme-analytics.com (that's the team inbox); Tom Lee (cc'd) is the procurement lead and will run vendor setup.
- Vendor forms: We use an internal vendor portal (https://vendorportal.acme-analytics.com). We prefer all documents uploaded there so finance can validate banking details.
- PO vs card: We primarily use PO for vendors > $5k/month and issue net-30 invoices. For initial pilots < $5k, we can pay by corporate card.
- Marketplace: We'd prefer to transact directly with Redwood rather than via AWS Marketplace for now (avoids extra fees), but if being on Marketplace speeds procurement, we can discuss.

Action items for Redwood: please upload vendor packet + W-9 to our portal or confirm you can provide bank details via a secure form. Also confirm whether Redwood requires a signed MSA or if the SOW is sufficient for a pilot.

Thanks,
Sophie
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Analytics
procurement@acme-analytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement intake & vendor setup — next steps (PO vs card)

Hi Sophie —

Great — thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers and plan: 

- We can upload the vendor packet and W-9 to your portal. However, your portal requires an account. Can you either (a) create a vendor portal account for Redwood (contact: vendors@redwood.com) or (b) share a secure upload link?
- Banking details: we don't share bank account numbers over email. If your portal supports bank/ACH uploads, that's preferred. Alternatively, we can provide a secure DocuSign form for banking information (I can send that).
- Legal/Commercial: For pilots under $5k we typically execute a short SOW and use our standard Terms (linked in the SOW). For larger engagements we'll sign an MSA + SOW. I'll attach the draft SOW (SOW-draft.docx).

Sean (cc) will help with invoice flow and payment terms. Dev (cc) is our Finance Operations lead — looping him in on bank details and invoice delivery.

Next steps from our side:
- I will upload Redwood_Vendor_Packet_v1.pdf and Redwood_W-9.pdf to your portal if you create the vendor account or send the secure link.
- If Tom prefers, I can open a DocuSign for the SOW so legal can review and sign quickly.

Which would you prefer? If you want us to create the DocuSign, confirm the recipient email for signature (procurement@acme-analytics.com or Tom directly).

Best,
Marissa
